newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sacks four high-ranking military officers.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sacks four high-ranking military officers.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin dismissed four senior military commanders on Friday, including the head of Russia's land forces, the Kremlin said.
A spokesman gave no reason for the sackings but Russian news agencies quoted sources as saying all four had been accused of abusing their positions.
General Vladimir Semyonov, the commander-in-chief of land forces, had already been suspended in November after accusations of committing "actions incompatible with his post".
The other three officers sacked under a Yeltsin decree included Colonel General Anton Terentyev, Semyonov's first deputy in charge of training.
Also dismissed were Admiral Igor Khmelnov, chief of the navy's general staff and Vice Admiral Vyacheslav Kharnikov, First Deputy Commander of the Northern Fleet.
The Kremlin spokesman said Yeltsin's decree stated only that they were dismissed and gave no explanation.
But Interfax news agency said: "According to information received by Interfax, A. Terentyev, I. Khmelnov and V. Kharnikov have been accused of abuse of their official positions."
Itar-Tass news agency also quoted sources as saying all four had been accused of misuse of office.
Semyonov said he planned to sue Defence Minister Igor Rodionov who, he said, was behind his dismissal.
Yeltsin plans to overhaul the underfunded and demoralised armed forces and has declared war on corruption, which is rife in the military as in many other areas of Russian life.
Despite many promises to crack down on corruption in the past, few top officials have been charged or jailed.
